plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $15. This means bidding $15.00 ensures I maximize expected value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item when I would have profited. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me. With no prior history and a single round, following the dominant strategy seems most rational.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $36. This is because:
1. Bidding less risks losing the item when I could have won
2. Bidding more than my value guarantees a potential loss
3. In a first-price sealed bid auction with independent values, bidding my true value maximizes expected profit
4. I have no prior history to adjust my strategy
5. The values are randomly drawn, so past rounds are irrelevant

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $42. This eliminates the risk of strategic underbidding (which could cause me to lose a prize worth more than my bid) or overbidding (which could cause me to pay more than the item's worth to me). Since this is a single round with no repeated interaction, there's no complex strategic consideration beyond bidding my true value.
